# Xu Programming Language

> Xu is a systems language for operating system and AI development. It provides custom native AOT backends, inferred ownership, and zero-GC execution.

Official website: https://xulang.org
Language repository: https://github.com/xulang-org/xu
Selected released SDK: 0.14.1
License: MIT (see the repository LICENSE; preserve third-party notices).

## Language and safety model

Xu uses static typing, ownership inference, borrow checking, and deterministic resource cleanup. It uses custom AOT backends rather than LLVM. Coroutines start with `xu f()` and communicate through typed channels. There is no garbage collector.

Ownership and borrow diagnostics constrain value use and mutable access. Shared mutable state in concurrent code still requires appropriate synchronization. Native code, FFI, and concurrent libraries have their own safety requirements; this is not a blanket guarantee against every data race or undefined behavior. See https://xulang.org/docs/lang/memory/ and https://xulang.org/docs/lang/concurrency/.

Parameters, fields, and receivers use `name Type`, without a colon. Bindings use `name := value`, with a `$` prefix (`$name := value`) for reassignment; `$&T` is an exclusive borrow. `<<` returns, `>>>` throws, and `>>> (err) { ... }` (or `>>>`) handles errors. Error text is obtained with `err.msg()`.

## Essential syntax cheat sheet & anti-hallucination rules

When answering questions about or generating Xu code:
- **No colons in declarations**: Use `fn add(a int, b int) int` and `name Type`, never `a: int` or `name: Type`.
- **Bindings and reassignment**. Declare a mutable binding with `$name := value` and reassign it with `name = new_value`.
- **Return and Throw**: Use `<< expr` to return from a function (never `return expr`). Use `>>> err` to throw/propagate an error (never `throw err`). Use `<<< code` to exit the process with an exit status code.
- **Loop Control**: Use `<-` to break out of a loop (never `break`). Use `->` to continue to the next iteration (never `continue`).
- **Error Handling**: Use `val := may_fail() >>> (err) { << err }` (or `val := may_fail() >>>` to propagate) (never `try/catch` or `if err != nil`). Obtain the error message string with `err.msg()`.
- **Borrowing**: `&T` denotes a shared read-only borrow; `$&T` denotes an exclusive mutable borrow.
- **Coroutines and Channels**: Start coroutines with `xu f()` (never `go f()`). Create typed channels with `chan Type{cap: N}`. Send with `ch <- value`, receive with `val := <-ch`.
- **Imports**: Standard library imports use a leading `#` (e.g. `#fmt`, `#strings`, `#net/http`, `#io`, `#time`, `#sync`).

## Complete examples

Save each block in its own `main.xu`, then run `xu check main.xu` and `xu run main.xu`. These examples share their sources with the site playground and the bundled official error-handling example.

### Hello world

```xu
@main

fn main() int {
    println("Hello from XU Programming Language!")
    << 0
}
```

### Coroutines and channels

Use `chan int{cap: N}`, `ch <- value` to send, and `<-ch` to receive. The example collects three results before exiting.

```xu
@main

fn main() int {
    results := chan int{cap: 3}
    xu worker(1, results)
    xu worker(2, results)
    xu worker(3, results)

    $total := 0
    for i in 0:3 {
        value := <-results
        total += value
    }
    println(total)
    << 0
}

fn worker(id int, results chan int) {
    results <- id * 10
}
```

### Error handling

```xu
@main

#errors

fn read_name(ok bool) string {
    if !ok {
        >>> errors.new("empty name")
    }
    << "ada"
}

fn load_or_fallback(ok bool) string {
    << read_name(ok) >>> (err) {
        println(err.msg())
        << "fallback"
    }
}

fn main() int {
    s := load_or_fallback(false)
    println(s)

    t := read_name(true) >>> (err) {
        println(err.msg())
        << 1
    }
    println(t)
    << 0
}
```

## Tools and package installation

- `xu build main.xu -o app`: compile a native executable.
- `xu run main.xu`: compile and execute.
- `xu check main.xu`: check syntax, types, and ownership.
- `xu debug main.xu`: build with debug information and launch LLDB, with GDB as fallback; an installed debugger is required.
- `xu test test.example.xu -v`: execute tests. Test and benchmark functions belong in `test.<name>.xu`, in `@main`, without parameters or return types.
- `xu fmt main.xu`: format source.
- `xu lsp`: serve LSP over stdin/stdout. Completion mainly covers keywords, built-ins, and current-file declarations. References use identifier text matching in the current file and same-directory Xu files; rename edits only the current file. Review edits for unrelated identifiers with the same spelling.
- `xu install`: resolve dependencies already declared in `xu.xun`, populate `vendor/`, and write `xu.lock`.
- `xu get <module>@<version>`: syntax template for adding a dependency with a verified published SemVer tag. Replace both placeholders. A module's declared version does not establish that a matching Git tag exists.
- `xu native`: compile/archive native modules, pack `.xulib` slices, and inspect/extract them. One-step static linking with `xu build`/`xu run` currently supports `macos-arm64` and `macos-x64` only. Other targets require object emission, conversion, and external linking.

Use the official packages bundled with the selected SDK, or the matching immutable source commit documented at https://xulang.org/docs/packages/. External imports use an explicit alias and full module path, for example `redis #github.com/xulang-org/packages/redis`. Standard-library and local-package imports have separate resolution rules (`#fmt`, `#util`). Redis connections use `redis.open`, `open_auth`, or `open_url`; consult the API for exact signatures. SQLite requires a prepared native bridge and the target's native toolchain.

## SDK, playground, and development scope

The browser playground implements a language subset with cooperative channel scheduling. Real multithreading, networking, C FFI, and desktop UI require the native SDK. See https://xulang.org/playground/ for the current sandbox limits.

Operating system development uses the released freestanding toolchain. Build ELF64 kernels with `--profile=freestanding` and `--target=x64-none`, `arm64-none`, or `riscv64-none`. The `examples/baremetal/kernel_poc` source covers explicit memory layout, hardware I/O, interrupts, and task context switching. See https://xulang.org/docs/os/.

Local AI inference and numerical computing span four layers in Xu: `#tensor` provides F16/BF16/FP8 encodings (`dequant_f16_to_f32`, `dequant_bf16_to_f32`), GGML `Q4Block`/`Q5Block`/`Q8Block`/`Q4KBlock`/`Q5KBlock`/`Q6KBlock` decoders + `Q8_K` integer K-quant helpers (`quantize_q8_k_row`, `dot_q4_k_q8_k_row_f32`, `dot_q5_k_q8_k_row_f32`, `dot_q6_k_q8_k_row_f32`) with zero-copy row dot helpers (`dot_*_row_f32`, `quantize_q5_0_row`), strided `TensorView` (`reshape`, `permute`, `read_f32_bytes`, `write_f32_bytes`), and 37 pure-Xu primitives (`src/tensor/ops.xu`, including `add_rmsnorm_f32`, `topk_f32`, `moe_router_f32`, `rope_yarn_f32`, `topk_cosine_f32`, `rope_interleaved_f32`, `geglu_f32`, `log_softmax_f32`, `cross_entropy_grad_f32`, `adamw_step_f32`, `lora_add_f32`, `lora_backward_f32`, `rmsnorm_backward_f32`, `layernorm_backward_f32`, `swiglu_backward_f32`, `softmax_backward_f32`, `grad_clip_norm_f32`); `--tensor-fusion` / `XU_TENSOR_FUSION=1` (with optional `--tensor-fast-math` / `XU_TENSOR_FAST_MATH=1`) lowers pure-Xu tensor loops to ARM64 NEON/SDOT and x86-64 SSE2/SSSE3 kernels (including `__xu_tensor_vsub_f32`, `__xu_tensor_vmul_f32`, `gemm4x8_q8_0_p4k4` parity, and `head_dim=128` paged attention); `examples/llm_engine/main.xu` loads HuggingFace model directories (`config.json` + single/sharded `model.safetensors.index.json` + `tokenizer.json`, F32/F16/BF16/FP8), single-file `Safetensors`, PEFT `--lora` adapters (`train-lora` pure-Xu fine-tuning with `--max-grad-norm` & SafeTensors export), lossless `--draft` speculative decoding, and mixed `Q4_K_M` & `Q5_K` `GGUF` (`--q8k-act` integer activation dots, DeepSeek-V2/V3/R1 MLA, full MoE 3D packed & split experts + shared experts, YaRN NTK-by-parts RoPE scaling, Gemma-2/Qwen3 metadata), quantized `--kv-dtype`, SentencePiece + GPT-2 BPE merges, $O(L)$ sampling with `logit_bias`, and multi-slot continuous-batching HTTP `serve` exposing both OpenAI (`/v1/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions` with `<think>` `reasoning_content` sync+SSE & SSE `delta.tool_calls`, stateful `POST /v1/responses` with `instructions`/`previous_response_id`/`tools`/SSE, batch `/v1/embeddings`) and Anthropic (`/v1/messages` sync+SSE & `x-api-key` auth); and `github.com/xulang-org/packages` (`v1.9.0`, 37 packages) provides `metal` GPU decode (176 symbols, 6 `.xulib` slices, `Q5KMatrix`, `gemv_q5_k_f32`, `moe_gemv_q5_k_f32`, `paged_kv_cache_append_f16`, `gemm_f32_tn`, `paged_attention_decode_f16`, `moe_gemv_q4_k_f32`/`moe_gemv_q6_k_f32`, `lora_add_f32`/`adamw_step_f32`/`cross_entropy_grad_f32`/`rmsnorm_backward_f32`/`swiglu_backward_f32`, `Q5Matrix`/`Q6KMatrix`, `rope_yarn_f32`, fused `moe_gemv_q4_0_f32`/`moe_gemv_q8_0_f32`, FlashAttention/FlashDecode, `add_rmsnorm_f32`, `geglu_f32`, `silu_f32`, `log_softmax_f32`, `moe_topk_f32`, `moe_weighted_add_f32`) plus pure-Xu `openai` (`clone_client`, Chat, Responses `/v1/responses` sync+SSE & `input_json`, Completions, Embeddings), `anthropic` (`clone_client`, vision `image_base64_block`/`image_url_block`, prompt caching `cache_control`/`cache_system`), `gemini` (Google Gemini REST API + `clone_client` + `batch_embed`), `mcp` (bidirectional stdio & Streamable HTTP with `ToolAnnotations`, `add_resource_template_handler`, `completion/complete`, `logging/setLevel`), `agent` (`Agent`, `ResponsesAgent`, `AnthropicAgent`, `GeminiAgent`, stateful sessions incl. `ResponsesSession`, `set_tool_hook` guardrails, `set_max_total_tokens` budget, streaming `AgentEvent`, `set_parallel_tools`), `rag` (`delete_doc`, `chunk_markdown`, MMR `search_mmr`, filtered BM25/RRF `search_bm25_filtered`/`search_hybrid_filtered`, `search_by_meta`/`search_hybrid_by_meta`, `rerank_hits`), `qdrant`, `milvus`, and `chroma` packages. See https://xulang.org/docs/ai/.

XACP documentation describes the language repository's development branch, separately from the selected released SDK. The implementation includes stdio and loopback TCP control. With a registered Screen, `ui.record` performs bounded XAR1 sampling within one request and returns `mode`, `records`, `bytes`, `truncated`, and quoted `payload`. It requires positive `win` and `mode: events|frames`, with optional `max_bytes`, `max_records`, and `duration_ms`. Clients pull successive segments by repeating requests, with one response per request, sequence numbers restarting at 1, and no persistent recorder or continuation cursor. `events` observes current `window/canvas/generation/open` state with `state=true`, without an input event log; `frames` exports dimensions only with `redacted=true`, without pixels. Sampling does not inject input or pump the application's event loop. `stream_required` is reserved for adapters without a sink/sampling capability; the supplied Screen sampling path does not return it. CLI `xu xacp record` captures stdout, separately from `ui.record`. See https://xulang.org/api/xacp/#ui-record and the authoritative dev protocol §7 at https://github.com/xulang-org/xu/blob/dev/examples/xacp/PROTOCOL.md#7-screenshots-mutations-and-recording. `xu xacp debug` inspects and launches a program; source debugging uses `xu debug`.

## Benchmark evidence

The published dashboard contains 60 display groups with 72 measured workload variants across 6 platforms, measured with Xu 0.14.1 on 2026-11-25. Each algorithm and input size retains its own source and results; display groups do not combine measurements. The measurement identity is independent of the selected SDK. See https://xulang.org/benchmarks/ and the source CI run: https://github.com/xulang-org/bench/actions/runs/45679539741. Consult the dashboard's per-platform results and methodology rather than infer a universal speedup.

## Additional syntax examples

Each block is a complete independent program from the site's playground examples or ownership tutorial. Save one at a time as `main.xu`.

### Bindings and mutability

```xu
@main

const MAX = 100

fn main() int {
    name := "Xu"
    $age := 20
    age += 1
    println(name)
    println(age)
    println(MAX)
    << 0
}
```

### Structs and methods

```xu
@main

fn main() int {
    $counter := Counter{n: 10}
    println(counter.get())
    counter.inc()
    println(counter.get())
    << 0
}

struct Counter {
    n int
}

fn (c Counter) get() int {
    << c.n
}

fn (c $&Counter) inc() {
    c.n += 1
}
```

### Borrowing

`&T` denotes a shared borrow; `$&T` denotes an exclusive mutable borrow. Follow compiler diagnostics for inferred ownership and borrow lifetimes.

```xu
@main

fn take(s string) {
    println(s)
}

fn len_of(s &string) int {
    << s.len
}

fn append_bang(s $&string) {
    s.push_str("!")
}

fn main() int {
    msg := "hello"
    println(len_of(&msg))
    println(msg)

    $owned := "hi"
    append_bang($&owned)
    println(owned)

    take(owned)
    // owned 已 move，不可再使用
    << 0
}
```

### Loops and control flow

`<-` breaks a loop and `->` continues it. `<<` returns from a function; `<<<` exits the process.

```xu
@main

fn main() int {
    for i in 0:10 {
        if i >= 7 { <- }
        if i % 2 == 0 { -> }
        println(i)
    }
    << 0
}
```

## Project manifest and dependency workflow

Place the project beside the extracted SDK directory named `xu-v0.14.1`, or adjust the local path below to the installed SDK's packages directory:

```xun
module: myapp
version: !ver 0.1.0
xu: !ver 0.14.1
require:
  "github.com/xulang-org/packages": file:../xu-v0.14.1/packages
```

From the project root, run:

```sh
xu install
xu check main.xu --offline
xu build main.xu --frozen -o app
```

Commit the application manifest and lockfile for reproducibility. For fetching the SDK's exact source commit instead of using a local bundle, follow https://xulang.org/docs/packages/. Native bridge artifacts may require separate preparation; installing Xu source dependencies does not build those artifacts.

## Tests

Save this as `test.example.xu`:

```xu
@main

fn test_add() {
    assert(1 + 1 == 2)
}
```

Run `xu test test.example.xu -v`. Benchmark functions follow the same filename and signature restrictions, use the `bench_` prefix, and are selected with `-bench REGEXP`.

## Native container metadata

The product `xu native pack` writes top-level `abi`, `format`, `module`, and `slices` metadata. Export signatures are stored in each slice's XUOBJ metadata. The source-tree Python helper `scripts/xunative.py` also retains fields copied from its input manifest, including `exports`; consumers must not assume every product-generated container has top-level `exports`.

Packing multiple target slices and linking a native executable are separate capabilities. The one-step macOS link path needs the macOS C toolchain. For other targets, emit XUOBJ with `--emit-obj`, convert to a platform object, and use the target's external linker. See https://xulang.org/docs/native/ for platform scope.

## Local AI inference and numerical APIs

These features are available in Xu 0.14.1 using the matching compiler and standard library. In the Xu source repository, set `XU` to your installed or built compiler and build from the repository root.

```sh
XU_STDLIB_ROOT="$PWD/src" "$XU" build --tensor-fusion examples/llm_engine/main.xu -o llm_engine
# (or XU_TENSOR_FUSION=1 XU_TENSOR_FAST_MATH=1; --tensor-fast-math unlocks fast reductions)
```

On macOS ARM64, sign the executable locally with `codesign -fs - ./llm_engine` before running it.

```sh
./llm_engine generate ./model.gguf 'ids:1,7,42' 16 0 40 --ctx 128 --kv-dtype f16 --top-p 900 --min-p 50 --repeat-penalty 1100 --presence-penalty 100 --frequency-penalty 50 --seed 42
./llm_engine serve ./model.gguf 127.0.0.1:8080 --kv-dtype bf16 --max-slots 4 --api-key secret
```

The `#tensor` module provides `F16`, `BF16`, four `FP8` variants (`Fp8E4M3Fn`, `Fp8E5M2`, `Fp8E4M3Fnuz`, `Fp8E5M2Fnuz`), `dequant_f16_to_f32`, `dequant_bf16_to_f32`, `TensorView` (`reshape`, `permute`, `read_f32_bytes`, `write_f32_bytes`), `Q4Block`/`Q5Block`/`Q8Block`/`Q4KBlock`/`Q5KBlock`/`Q6KBlock` (`read_q4_k`, `read_q5_k`, `read_q6_k`, `Q8_K_BYTES`, `dot_*_bytes_f32`, `dot_*_row_f32`, `quantize_q5_0_row`, `quantize_q8_k_row`, `dot_q4_k_q8_k_row_f32`, `dot_q5_k_q8_k_row_f32`, `dot_q6_k_q8_k_row_f32`), and 37 pure-Xu primitives (`dot_f32`, `axpy_f32`, `vadd_f32`, `vsub_f32`, `vmul_f32`, `vscale_f32`, `silu_f32`, `gelu_f32`, `rmsnorm_f32`, `add_rmsnorm_f32`, `layernorm_f32`, `l2_normalize_f32`, `cosine_similarity_f32`, `topk_cosine_f32`, `softmax_f32`, `log_softmax_f32`, `swiglu_f32`, `geglu_f32`, `moe_router_f32`, `rope_f32`, `rope_interleaved_f32`, `rope_yarn_f32`, `matvec_f32`, `matmul_f32`, `argmax_f32`, `topk_f32`, `quantize_q8_0`, `quantize_q4_0_row`, `cross_entropy_grad_f32`, `adamw_step_f32`, `lora_add_f32`, `lora_backward_f32`, `rmsnorm_backward_f32`, `layernorm_backward_f32`, `swiglu_backward_f32`, `softmax_backward_f32`, `grad_clip_norm_f32`). On `examples/llm_engine/main.xu`, the engine loads HuggingFace model directories (`config.json`, single or sharded `model.safetensors.index.json`, `tokenizer.json`, `tokenizer_config.json`, F32/F16/BF16/FP8), single-file Safetensors, PEFT SafeTensors LoRA adapters (`--lora`, `--lora-scale`), pure-Xu `train-lora` fine-tuning (`--lora-rank`, `--lora-alpha`, `--steps`, `--lr`, `--max-grad-norm`), lossless target-verified speculative decoding (`--draft`, `--draft-k`), and compatible GGUF v2/v3 (mixed `Q4_K_M` & `Q5_K` with `Q4_K`/`Q5_K`/`Q6_K` and `--q8k-act` integer K-quant dots, F32/F16/BF16/FP8/Q4_0/`Q5_0`/`Q8_0` `p4k4` SIMD, DeepSeek-V2/V3/R1 MLA with `kv_lora_rank`/`q_lora_rank`/`qk_nope_head_dim`/`qk_rope_head_dim`/`v_head_dim`, full MoE 3D packed & split experts + shared experts, YaRN RoPE scaling, and GGUF metadata), supports optional `qk_norm`, auto-detected multi-template chat (ChatML, Llama-3, Gemma, Mistral), paged KV caches in F32/F16/BF16/FP8 (`--kv-dtype`), SentencePiece + GPT-2 BPE merges, $O(L)$ sampling (`--min-p`, `--presence-penalty`, `--frequency-penalty`, unbounded `top_k`, `logit_bias`), and a multi-slot continuous-batching HTTP server serving OpenAI (`/v1/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions` with `<think>` `reasoning_content` sync+SSE, `tools` -> `tool_calls` sync + SSE `delta.tool_calls`, `response_format`, `logprobs`, stateful `POST /v1/responses` with `instructions`/`previous_response_id`/`tools`/SSE, batch `/v1/embeddings`) and Anthropic Messages API (`/v1/messages` sync+SSE with `thinking`/`text`/`tool_use` + `tool_result` and `x-api-key` auth).

`--tensor-fusion` / `XU_TENSOR_FUSION=1` enables pattern matching for eligible Xu loops on optimized native ARM64 (NEON/SDOT) and x64 (SSE2/SSSE3) targets. Use Xu loops in application code. The compiler manages the `__xu_tensor_*` helpers (including `__xu_tensor_vsub_f32`, `__xu_tensor_vmul_f32`, `gemm4x8_q8_0_p4k4` parity, and paged attention across `head_dim % 4 == 0`). `--tensor-fast-math` / `XU_TENSOR_FAST_MATH=1` permits floating-point reassociation or fused multiply-add in eligible kernels, which can change low bits. On macOS, `github.com/xulang-org/packages` (`v1.9.0`, 37 packages) provides `metal` GPU compute (176 symbols across 6 `.xulib` slices, `gemm_f32_tn`, `paged_kv_cache_append_f16`, `paged_attention_decode_f16`, `gemv_q5_k_f32`, `moe_gemv_q4_k_f32`/`moe_gemv_q5_k_f32`/`moe_gemv_q6_k_f32`, `lora_add_f32`/`adamw_step_f32`/`cross_entropy_grad_f32`/`rmsnorm_backward_f32`/`swiglu_backward_f32`, `Q4Matrix`/`Q5Matrix`/`Q8Matrix`/`Q4KMatrix`/`Q5KMatrix`/`Q6KMatrix`, `simd_sum`/`simd_max` norms/softmax/quant GEMV, online FlashAttention `causal_attention_f32`/`f16` & FlashDecode `attention_decode_f32`/`f16`, `rope_interleaved_f32`, `rope_yarn_f32`, `kv_cache_append_f16`, `add_rmsnorm_f32`, `geglu_f32`, `silu_f32`, `log_softmax_f32`, `moe_topk_f32`, `moe_weighted_add_f32`, fused `moe_gemv_q4_0_f32`/`moe_gemv_q8_0_f32`), alongside pure-Xu `openai` (`clone_client`, Chat, Responses `/v1/responses` sync+SSE `responses`/`responses_stream` & structured `input_json`, vision `ContentPart`, `json_schema_format`, `extra_body_json`, `/v1/completions`, retries, streaming `tool_calls` merge, `reasoning_content`), `anthropic` (`clone_client`, `/v1/messages`, vision `image_base64_block`/`image_url_block`, prompt caching `cache_control`/`cache_system`, `thinking_delta`, chunked `tool_use`, `429`/`529` retries), `gemini` (Google Gemini `clone_client`, `generate`/`generate_stream`/`embed`/`batch_embed`, `inline_data_part`, `functionCall`, `thoughts`, `response_schema_json`), bidirectional `mcp` (JSON-RPC 2.0 `2025-03-26` stdio & Streamable HTTP clients/servers, `ToolAnnotations`, `ResourceTemplateInfo`, `add_resource_template_handler`, `completion/complete`, `logging/setLevel`/`set_logging_level`, `clone_client`, `close_session`, SSE negotiation), `agent` (`Agent` + `ResponsesAgent` + `AnthropicAgent` + `GeminiAgent`, stateful `Session`/`ResponsesSession`/`AnthropicSession`/`GeminiSession`, `set_tool_hook` guardrails, `set_max_total_tokens` budgets, `AgentEvent` `run_stream*`/`send_stream*`, `set_parallel_tools(bool)` via `xu` goroutines, `Step.is_error`), and `rag` (`delete_doc`, `chunk_text`, `chunk_markdown`, `MemoryStore` with dense `topk_cosine_f32`, metadata-filtered `search_by_meta`/`search_hybrid_by_meta`, `rerank_hits`, MMR `search_mmr`, sparse Okapi BM25 `search_bm25`/`search_bm25_filtered`, and RRF hybrid `search_hybrid`/`search_hybrid_filtered`/`retrieve_hybrid`, `save_json`/`load_json`).

- With `#math`, `math.float16_to_f32(h int) f32` converts the IEEE 754 binary16 bit pattern in the low 16 bits of `h`. The pattern `0x3e00` converts to `1.5`. See https://xulang.org/api/math/#preview-float16_to_f32.
- `slice.reserve(n int)` is a built-in method on a mutable dynamic slice. It reserves capacity for at least `n` elements and preserves length and values. Pass a nonnegative element count. See https://xulang.org/api/slices/#reserve.
- `slice.resize_zero(n int)` is a built-in method on a mutable dynamic slice of integers, floats, or booleans. It preserves the prefix, zero-initializes the added elements when growing, and retains capacity when shrinking. See https://xulang.org/api/slices/#resize_zero.

## Standard library and integrations

The API catalog at https://xulang.org/api/ is generated from the selected released SDK. It covers formatting, errors, collections, text and encodings, files and processes, networking, cryptography, SQL, and the `ui`, `ui/draw`, `ui/layout`, `ui/widgets`, and `ui/webview` packages. Consult each package's documented target limits.

### Standard library package directory

- `#fmt`: Formatted I/O, string formatting, `println`, `sprint`
- `#strings`: UTF-8 string manipulation, splitting, trimming, and searching
- `#bytes`: Byte buffer operations, slice manipulations, and dynamic buffers
- `#strconv`: String conversion to int, float, bool, and numeric formatting
- `#unicode`: Unicode UTF-8 and UTF-16 character classifications and conversions
- `#regexp`: Regular expressions parsing and pattern matching
- `#net`: TCP, UDP, raw IP socket networking, `listen_on`, `dial`, `listen_packet`
- `#net/http`: High-concurrency multi-worker HTTP server and client, HTTP/2 HPACK decoding
- `#io`: Stream primitives, Reader/Writer interfaces, and filesystem abstractions
- `#os`: System calls, process spawning, signals, environment variables
- `#sync`: Mutex, WaitGroup, Once, and atomic primitives
- `#time`: Wall-clock time, monotonic duration, timers, tickers, and sleep
- `#runtime`: Compiler runtime statistics, allocator inspection, coroutine scheduling
- `#database/sql`: SQL driver interfaces and connection pooling
- `#crypto/sm4`, `#crypto/sm2`, `#crypto/sm3`, `#crypto/sm9`, `#crypto/zuc`: ShangMi national standard algorithms
- `#crypto/aes`, `#crypto/rsa`, `#crypto/sha256`, `#crypto/tls`: International cryptographic algorithms and TLS
- `#ui`, `#ui/widgets`, `#ui/draw`, `#ui/layout`, `#ui/webview`: Declarative retained-mode UI and GPU canvas

### Networking patterns (TCP / UDP)

```xu
@main
#net

fn run_tcp_server() {
    ln := net.listen_on("tcp", "127.0.0.1:8080") >>> (err) { << }
    c := ln.accept() >>> (err) { << }
    buf := c.read(4096) >>> (err) { << }
    c.write(&buf) >>> (err) { << }
}
```

Official service integrations live in the independent https://github.com/xulang-org/packages repository. The website documents the SDK's pinned package snapshot, which can differ from that repository's current branch. Read the relevant API and example before assuming a protocol feature or native target is supported.
